result.summary: The image shows a standard urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and traffic signals. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, sightlines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles near the corners, and the crossing distance remains unprotected by curb extensions.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection crosswalks may block the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a commercial urban street with a signalized intersection and high-visibility crosswalk markings. hazards.description: While a traffic light is present, no dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time remaining.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow, mixed-use urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While the environment is pedestrian-oriented with active street life, safety is compromised by visual obstructions from parked cars and outdoor dining structures that narrow the walkway and block sightlines.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and outdoor dining structures located immediately adjacent to the crosswalk block the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbsides near the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Sidewalk Narrowing
hazards.description: Outdoor dining furniture and planters significantly reduce the effective clear width of the sidewalk, potentially forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility 'Yield to Pedestrian' signage to clearly mark the crossing point for drivers.
